questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Nutrition programmes, food fortification & food hygiene
questions.stem: The reference protein against which protein quality is measured is:
options: Egg protein, with a biological value near 100
questions.concept: Biological value reflects the proportion of absorbed nitrogen retained. Cereal proteins are limiting in lysine and pulse proteins in methionine, so the traditional cereal-pulse combination is mutually supplementary.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Nutrition programmes, food fortification & food hygiene
questions.stem: Mid-upper arm circumference below 11.5 cm in a child aged 6 to 59 months indicates:
questions.concept: MUAC is age-independent between 1 and 5 years and is the simplest community screening tool, used with bilateral pedal oedema and weight-for-height to identify severe acute malnutrition.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Nutrition programmes, food fortification & food hygiene
questions.stem: Kwashiorkor is distinguished from marasmus by:
options: Presence of oedema with relatively preserved subcutaneous fat
questions.concept: Kwashiorkor shows oedema, flaky paint dermatosis, hair changes and fatty liver with a miserable apathetic child, whereas marasmus shows extreme wasting with an alert, ravenously hungry child.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Nutrition programmes, food fortification & food hygiene
questions.stem: The staple food fortification programme in India includes fortifying salt with:
options: Iodine, and increasingly with both iodine and iron
questions.concept: Universal salt iodisation is one of the most successful public health interventions in India. Oil is fortified with vitamins A and D, wheat flour and rice with iron, folic acid and B12, and milk with vitamins A and D.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Nutrition programmes, food fortification & food hygiene
questions.stem: Lathyrism results from prolonged consumption of:
options: Lathyrus sativus (khesari dal) containing BOAA neurotoxin
questions.concept: It causes spastic paraparesis in young adults. Epidemic dropsy comes from argemone-contaminated mustard oil and aflatoxicosis from Aspergillus-contaminated groundnuts and maize.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Nutrition programmes, food fortification & food hygiene
questions.stem: The mid-day meal scheme aims principally to:
options: Improve nutritional status and school enrolment, attendance and retention
questions.concept: It supplies a defined minimum of calories and protein on school days, with the dual educational and nutritional objective, and is now the PM POSHAN scheme.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Nutrition programmes, food fortification & food hygiene
questions.stem: Pasteurisation of milk by the holder method involves heating to:
options: 63 degrees Celsius for 30 minutes followed by rapid cooling
questions.concept: The flash or HTST method uses 72 degrees for 15 seconds. The phosphatase test confirms adequate pasteurisation, as the enzyme is destroyed under the same conditions as pathogens.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Nutrition programmes, food fortification & food hygiene
questions.stem: Food poisoning with an incubation period under six hours and prominent vomiting suggests:
options: Preformed toxin of Staphylococcus aureus or Bacillus cereus
questions.concept: Short incubation indicates preformed toxin, whereas 12 to 48 hours indicates infection requiring bacterial multiplication, as with Salmonella. Botulism has a longer incubation with neurological features.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Nutrition programmes, food fortification & food hygiene
questions.stem: The most reliable index of chronic undernutrition in a community is:
questions.concept: Stunting reflects long-term cumulative deprivation, wasting reflects acute recent deficit, and underweight combines both. Stunting is largely irreversible after the first 1000 days.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Nutrition programmes, food fortification & food hygiene
questions.stem: The first 1000 days of life, critical for nutrition intervention, spans:
options: Conception to two years of age
questions.concept: This window covers rapid brain and physical growth when deficits cause irreversible cognitive and stature deficits, which is why maternal nutrition, exclusive breastfeeding and timely complementary feeding are prioritised.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Non-communicable disease epidemiology: CVD, diabetes, cancer, tobacco
questions.stem: The leading cause of death in India today is:
questions.concept: India has undergone epidemiological transition, with non-communicable diseases now accounting for about 60% of deaths, though a double burden persists as communicable disease remains significant.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Non-communicable disease epidemiology: CVD, diabetes, cancer, tobacco
questions.stem: The most important modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease amenable to population intervention is:
questions.concept: Tobacco, unhealthy diet, physical inactivity and harmful alcohol use are the four shared behavioural risk factors underlying the major non-communicable diseases, making them the focus of population strategies.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Non-communicable disease epidemiology: CVD, diabetes, cancer, tobacco
questions.stem: Rose's population strategy of prevention argues that:
options: A small risk reduction across a whole population prevents more disease than targeting high-risk individuals
questions.concept: Most cases arise from the large number of people at modest risk rather than the few at high risk - the prevention paradox, which explains why population salt reduction outperforms treating hypertensives alone.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Non-communicable disease epidemiology: CVD, diabetes, cancer, tobacco
questions.stem: The National Programme for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Diseases and Stroke screens adults over 30 for:
questions.concept: Population-based screening includes oral, breast and cervical cancer along with hypertension and diabetes, delivered through Health and Wellness Centres by community health officers and ASHAs.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Non-communicable disease epidemiology: CVD, diabetes, cancer, tobacco
questions.stem: The commonest cancer among Indian women is:
options: Breast cancer, having overtaken cervical cancer
questions.concept: Among Indian men, oral cavity and lung cancers predominate, reflecting tobacco use in both smoked and smokeless forms. Cervical cancer remains second in women and is largely preventable.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Non-communicable disease epidemiology: CVD, diabetes, cancer, tobacco
questions.stem: Visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA) is used for cervical cancer screening in India because it:
options: Is low-cost, gives immediate results and can be done by trained health workers
questions.concept: Single-visit screen-and-treat with cryotherapy addresses the loss to follow-up that undermines cytology-based programmes in low-resource settings. HPV testing is increasingly preferred where affordable.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Non-communicable disease epidemiology: CVD, diabetes, cancer, tobacco
questions.stem: The Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act (COTPA) prohibits:
options: Smoking in public places, sale to minors and advertising of tobacco products
questions.concept: It also mandates pictorial health warnings covering 85% of the package. Taxation remains the single most effective measure for reducing consumption, particularly among the young and the poor.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Non-communicable disease epidemiology: CVD, diabetes, cancer, tobacco
questions.stem: Smokeless tobacco use in India is important because it:
options: Causes oral cancer and is highly prevalent, including among women
questions.concept: Gutka, khaini and zarda cause oral submucous fibrosis and gingivobuccal carcinoma - the Indian oral cancer. Smokeless use is far more prevalent among Indian women than smoking.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Non-communicable disease epidemiology: CVD, diabetes, cancer, tobacco
questions.stem: The WHO STEPS approach to non-communicable disease surveillance involves:
options: Sequential steps of questionnaire, physical measurement and biochemical assessment
questions.concept: The stepwise design lets countries implement surveillance at a level matched to their resources while retaining international comparability of the core data.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Non-communicable disease epidemiology: CVD, diabetes, cancer, tobacco
questions.stem: Diabetes prevalence in urban India compared with rural is:
options: Higher, reflecting sedentary lifestyle and dietary change
questions.concept: Indians develop diabetes at a younger age and lower BMI than Western populations, with greater visceral adiposity - the Asian Indian phenotype, which is why lower BMI cut-offs are used.
